classification.difficultyReason: Without intermediate scaffolding, identify and justify where a moving point gives the least and greatest spatial angle, then construct suitable right triangles to calculate both extrema.

content.prompt: $ABCDEFGH$ is a cube with sides of length $5\text{ cm}$. $P$ is a point on $BC$. Describe the location(s) of $P$ so that $\angle EPH$ is least or greatest, and state the size of $\angle EPH$ in each case, to two decimal places.

spec.description: Cube with P on rear upper edge BC and segments PE and PH. BF, FG and FE are concealed dashed edges.
spec.mathematics: All cube edges are 5 cm. P may vary along BC, including its endpoints.
spec.answerVisibility: No extremal positions or angle values supplied.

answer.short:
$P$ is at $B$ or $C$; $\angle EPH\approx35.26^\circ$.

The angle is smallest at either endpoint of $BC$.
answer.worked:
The angle subtended by the fixed edge $EH$ increases as $P$ moves from either endpoint of the parallel edge $BC$ towards its midpoint. Thus the least angle occurs at $B$ or $C$.
At $P=B$, triangle $EBH$ is right-angled at $E$, with $BE=5\sqrt2\text{ cm}$ and $EH=5\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle EBH&=\frac{EH}{BE}\\\tan\angle EBH&=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\\\angle EBH&\approx35.26^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The position $P=C$ gives the same angle by symmetry.

answer.short:
$P$ is the midpoint of $BC$; $\angle EPH\approx38.94^\circ$.

Use the symmetry of triangle $EPH$ at this position.
answer.worked:
The greatest angle occurs when $P$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $EH$. By symmetry, $PM$ bisects $\angle EPH$ and is perpendicular to $EH$.
The perpendicular separation $PM$ has horizontal and vertical components of $5\text{ cm}$ each:
$$\begin{align*}PM^2&=5^2+5^2\\PM&=5\sqrt2\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Also $EM=2.5\text{ cm}$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle EPM&=\frac{EM}{PM}\\\tan\angle EPM&=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\\\angle EPH&=2\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\right)\\\angle EPH&\approx38.94^\circ.\end{align*}$$
